title: Elon Musk's Neuralink is recruiting for 'Telepathy' brain-chip trial, here's how to apply
excerpt: The Neuralink tech ‘aims to enable people living with paralysis to control their computers using only their thoughts’
content:
Published 16:10 26 Nov 2026 GMT

The tech is set to become life-changing for people living with disabilities

Last year, Elon Musk’s Neuralink revealed that it had achieved a major breakthrough with its first patient to test out the neurotech firm’s chip.

Noland Arbaugh had the chip implanted into his brain back in January 2024, and is now able to use it to control things like a robotic arm to write or to play a video game.

The technology is set to become life-changing for people living with disabilities, and now Neuralink is recruiting for a brain-chip trial.

The firm’s Telepathy product ‘aims to enable people living with paralysis to control their computers using only their thoughts’, with the trial offering people the chance to undergo the surgery for themselves.

How does Neuralink Telepathy work?

According to the company, Neuralink ‘listens to the part of the brain that controls the hand’.

Elon Musk’s Neuralink revealed a major breakthrough with its first brain chip patient (Finn Gomez/Getty Images)

This means that people taking part in the study will learn to control a computer cursor through simply imagining moving their hand, with the imagined motions then being ‘calibrated into computer mouse actions’.

Neuralink goes on to explain: “Through their mind-controlled mouse, participants may be able to fully operate their computer.

“From messaging friends and family to watching videos, writing code, 3D modeling, creating art, and gaming, participants use Neuralink to potentially restore digital independence.”

The operation will involve a brain surgeon making a small opening in the skull, with a Neuralink R1 robot placing the implant’s thin, soft threads into the surface of the motor cortex.

The firm continues: “The implant fits into the opening in the skull, and the cut is closed. It sits under your scalp, with nothing cosmetically visible. It works wirelessly and charges through the skin.”

The tech is set to become life-changing for people living with disabilities (Neuralink)

How to apply for Neuralink’s trial

If you’re interested in applying to the trial, then you’ll first need to make sure you are eligible to participate.

Neuralink are specifically looking for individuals who have little or no use of both hands and arms due to Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), a spinal cord injury, or a brain stem stroke.

You must be at least 18 years old and have a consistent and reliable caregiver.

If you fit the bill, then you can fill out a brief online form where you will have the opportunity to tell the team about yourself and see whether the study may be a fit.

From there, a member of the study will be in touch to discuss further details as well as explain what taking part would mean for you and your caregivers, and answer your questions.
